title: HealthGraphBench: conditional contribution of relations and procedural complexity in regulatory health data
abstract: HealthGraphBench studies when relations provide predictive information beyond individual history and popularity, and what complexity is sufficient to exploit it. Three retrospective regulatory tasks distinguish comparisons of procedures, interventions on a step, and temporal confirmation that has not been performed. RC3.1 completes 75 new fits within caps, without retraining the retained BPR models. On Part D 2024, a cosine vote selected on validation achieves micro recall@10 of 0.258583 versus 0.236182 for BPR: difference +0.022401, conditional paired interval [0.014212;0.030800]. The gain is concentrated among peer-supported candidates; rare or weakly supported candidates show reversals. Selected GraphSAGE achieves 0.145970 under this procedure, without invalidating all architectures. In MAUDE, the real aggregation edges outperform a degree-preserving rewiring, but doubling fanout does not provide a consistent gain and BPR smoothing varies by period. In CMS, adding owners, even when restricted by a documentary proxy, does not restore a consistent gain over local history on the same inspections. Workload curves include units without positives and do not measure clinical utility. The intervals condition on fixed fits/configurations, without selection coverage or a simultaneous guarantee. The targets had already been consulted: the results are exploratory, not independent temporal confirmation or external human reproduction.

sections.heading: Question: relational information and procedural complexity
sections.latex:
Relations between entities may reflect a shared signal, common popularity, or a dependency already absorbed by individual history. Their presence therefore does not guarantee a predictive gain. The common question is: in which situations do relations provide predictive information beyond individual history and popularity, and what complexity is needed to exploit it?

We distinguish three objects: comparison of reasonably tuned procedures; interventions that isolate a step or factor within those procedures; and confirmation on a genuinely unconsulted target. RC3.1 performs the first two on periods already consulted. Locking the new calculations beforehand does not erase this exposure: all new analyses remain exploratory. Temporal confirmation and a study by a genuine external team have not been performed.

The opposition between ``graph'' and ``no graph'' would be misleading. A neighbor vote explicitly exploits links; BPR also learns from relations, without necessarily propagating messages at inference. Removing propagation or smoothing does not remove all relational information. Contrasts are therefore interpreted at the level of the procedures and steps actually modified, not as an exhaustive causal decomposition of information sources.

sections.heading: Related work and comparison conditions
sections.latex:
Open Graph Benchmark structures common tasks, splits, and metrics; RelBench and RelBench v2 extend relational prediction across multiple tables with temporal constraints\cite{hu2020ogb,robinson2024relbench,gu2026relbench}. Their benefits under their own conditions provide a counterpoint to any negative generalization from HealthGraphBench. We do not reproduce their rankings.

Simple baselines, candidate selection, and temporal aspects influence link comparisons\cite{huang2023tgb,poursafaei2022}. Here, MAUDE and Part D exclude links already known for the target entity; direct memorization therefore cannot suffice, but peer observations and popularity remain informative. Errica and colleagues motivate controlled protocols in the distinct domain of graph classification\cite{errica2020}: this reference is not evidence of the medical mechanisms studied here. Work on information leakage and REFORMS motivates explicit descriptions of targets, data, and limitations\cite{kapoor2023leakage,kapoor2024reforms}, without certifying compliance. The narrative review carried over from RC3 was closed on 29 September 2026; it is not a systematic review updated by this campaign.

sections.heading: Three tasks, populations, and data availability
sections.latex:
\paragraph{MAUDE.} The target is a product-code--problem-code link observed for the first time within the retained window, not an individual diagnosis. The clock is \texttt{DATE\_RECEIVED}, without a verified public availability date for each field. A product must have at least one prior report, the problem must exist globally in the past, and the link must be absent from the product's history. All eligible problems are ranked, without sampled evaluation negatives. Initial history spans 2019Q1--2022Q4; 2023 is validation and 2024--2025 are exploratory tests. States are refitted annually; history and candidates evolve after each evaluated quarter. Previously unseen vocabulary outside the history is not the target of this task\cite{hgbcontract,hgbcode}.

\paragraph{CMS nursing homes.} The target is a standard G--L deficiency during a retained Health Standard episode, defined by (CCN, date), with at least one prior inspection. Prediction is constructed retrospectively immediately before that episode: it is \emph{conditional on an inspection taking place}. It predicts neither the date nor the occurrence of an inspection and is not a national prioritization of facilities. The new preparation retains the same 23\,712 rows from 2019--2025 as Q2, the same facilities, local histories, and labels; only owner aggregates are recomputed. The pre-2023, pre-2024, and pre-2025 fits use only rows preceding the target year. An earlier association date does not guarantee that the link was then public or legally active; current extracts, unknown ownership end dates, and retained cycles limit reconstruction\cite{hgbcontract,hgbcode}.

\paragraph{Medicare Part D.} The retained Q2 preparation is declared as a verified derived input, not a new raw acquisition. The drug is the exact generic name after trimming leading and trailing whitespace, not an RxNorm concept. Each annual cohort contains 2\,000 previously observed prescribers, selected by the order (SHA-256 of NPI, NPI). History from 2019--2022 precedes validation in 2023, and 2019--2023 precedes the 2024 test. All drugs already observed globally in the cohort's history, except those already linked to the prescriber, are candidates. All 2\,000 prescribers are retained even without a new positive. A positive is a \emph{published and observable} link, not a first prescription. CMS suppression of combinations with at most ten claims prevents treating a published absence as a clinical negative\cite{cmspartd,hgbpartd}.

The event or service calendar is not a calendar of public access to file versions. All three domains are retrospective. No national representativeness, exhaustive clinical coverage, or statistical independence of a disjoint NPI cohort is established.

sections.heading: Common comparison, interventions, and conditional analyses
sections.latex:
\subsection{Part D: comparing procedures under a common contract}
Prescriber--drug histories are binary: similarities concern distinct drugs, not claim counts. For historical sets $D_i,D_j$, the three similarities are $|D_i\cap D_j|$, $|D_i\cap D_j|/|D_i\cup D_j|$, and $|D_i\cap D_j|/\sqrt{|D_i||D_j|}$. A candidate's score is the weighted vote $s_{m,k}(i,d)=\sum_{j\in N_{m,k}(i)}m(D_i,D_j)\,\mathbf{1}\{d\in D_j\}$. Neighbors have strictly positive similarity; self is excluded, and similarity ties follow lexical NPI order. The neighbor list is independent of the candidate. Final ties follow decreasing global support, then increasing canonical generic key.

Each similarity selects $k\in\{8,16,32,50,100,200\}$ on micro recall at ten proposals in 2023 validation. Mean-aggregation GraphSAGE is actually trained: dimensions 16/32 crossed with $L_2\in\{0.0005,0.000005,0\}$, thirty epochs, learning rate 0.02, and fanout 8. Node embeddings are trainable; the shared transformations and nonlinearity are those of the MAUDE backend adapted to the prescriber--drug bipartite graph. All configurations and the three seeds 103/211/307 are completed before selection on their mean; no favorable seed is chosen. An exact tie follows the published order. Choices are written before 2024 scoring.

BPR reuses, without retraining, the three Q2 states selected by its historical six-configuration grid: dimension 32, learning rate 0.03, $L_2=0.001$, five negatives, thirty epochs, and specialty weight 0.35. Compatibility of histories, mappings, cohorts, candidates, targets, and states is checked for the new consumption. Global popularity and specialty-specific popularity are fixed baselines. The primary contrast is selected cosine minus reused selected BPR, on 2024 micro recall@10. Six nominal opportunities imply neither identical computation nor identical objectives: BPR and GraphSAGE also differ in negatives, initialization, and auxiliary specialty information. Their difference does not isolate architecture.

\subsection{MAUDE: modifying one factor without removing relational labels}
The four GraphSAGE levels share dimension 16, $L_2=0.000005$, learning rate 0.02, thirty epochs, and the three seeds: fanout 4/8/16 on real adjacency, then fanout 8 on rewired aggregation adjacency. No level is selected after observing results. Bounded bipartite double-edge swaps use seed 303 and ten attempts per edge. They preserve degrees and types at the annual cutoff, not by quarter, while retaining labels, probe, negative-sampling CSR, initialization, and candidates. This is a diagnostic of the aggregation step, not a uniform null or medical causality; the training links remain present.

The selected annual Q2 BPR checkpoints (dimension 16, $L_2=0$) are reused. On the same learned tensors, raw inference $x\cdot y$ is compared with inference constructed using $0.5$ own vector $+0.5$ mean of one-hop historical neighbors. Inference representations are fixed at the annual origin. This contrast isolates inference post-processing, conditional on a configuration historically chosen with smoothing; it does not compare the best separately tuned raw and smoothed BPR models. The historical GraphSAGE control without propagation still learns links through its node vectors and BPR objective.

\subsection{CMS: the same inspections, different owner representations}
Local history is compared with history augmented by combined aggregates, then by a better-documented subset according to an operational proxy. The proxy retains combined PAC identifiers supported by a dated enrollment--CCN CHOW event and an owner association, both strictly before inspection; enrollment must refer to a single CCN among earlier events, and both endpoints of the peer link must qualify. It invents neither perfect name resolution nor an end date. The three representations share the new strict cutoff $<$; the historical Q2 $\leq$ remains unchanged in the sealed results.

Settings are shared without new selection: logistic regression $C=0.01$, LBFGS, at most 1\,000 iterations, tolerance $10^{-8}$, without class weighting; histogram-based boosted trees, learning rate 0.05, 100 iterations, at most 15 leaves, and $L_2=1$, without early stopping. States/scalers are learned on training data alone. Training sets have fewer than 200\,000 rows: these eighteen fits are deterministic, not three pseudo-replications. Sensitivity to the proxy is not causal evidence of link quality.

\subsection{Strata, uncertainty, and workload}
All strata are fixed from the past: historical distinct drugs in Part D ($\leq10$, 11--50, $>50$), MAUDE reports (1--9, 10--49, 50--199, 200+), historical candidate support ($\leq5$, 6--50, $>50$), and neighbor support (0, 1--2, 3+). Part D uses a fixed top50 cosine stratifier, independent of the method or selected $k$. CMS uses 1/2--3/$>3$ prior inspections and no combined association/none retained/some/all retained. Groups without a sufficient denominator or sufficient classes are undefined, not zero.

The paired bootstrap comprises 2\,000 draws, seed 313, by prescriber, product, or facility; all periods of an entity remain together. Hits are first averaged across seeds before the micro ratio, and seed ranges are separate. The 2.5--97.5\% percentiles are conditional on fixed fits and configurations; they do not cover selection and guarantee neither independence between periods/networks nor simultaneous coverage. The absolute margin 0.01 is a conventional analytical reference, not a clinical threshold. An upper bound below the margin does not by itself prove equivalence.

Workload is reported for $K=1,5,10,20,50,100$: published links recovered, precision among actually proposed slots $\min(K,\text{candidates})$, entity--period coverage, and fraction without positives. MAUDE expressly extends this calculation to all known product--quarters with support at least one and nonempty candidates, including those without positives. The absence of a published link is not a clinical error; these curves measure neither human time nor patient benefit. CMS remains conditional on inspection.

sections.heading: Retained results: context, not transfer of evidence
sections.latex:
The tables below retain the historical MAUDE/CMS/Part D results and intervals with their RC3 origins. They are neither replaced nor recalculated. Duration analyses C, propagation analyses D1, and tuned comparisons Q2 remain distinguished in the supplement. Historical three-epoch GraphSAGE is not the thirty-epoch RC3.1 GraphSAGE; no historical interval is attributed to the new fits.

The previous change in ranking with duration/configuration motivates the new diagnostics, without establishing that an old nearly flat loss was a bug. The RC3 top50 cosine baseline motivated the Part D comparison but is not retroactively added to Q2 tables: RC3.1 runs its own grid under the common contract. DOI \nolinkurl{10.5281/zenodo.22796551} identifies benchmark v0.2.0, not this manuscript or RC3.1\cite{hgb2026,hgbq2methods}.

sections.heading: Results: localized contribution, no universal winner
Interpretation: identifying the conditions for gain, then the minimum complexity
sections.latex:
Three observations conditionally answer the common question. In Part D, links between historical profiles provide a gain beyond popularity baselines and the retained BPR when candidates have sufficient local support; a normalized vote is sufficient to exploit it in the aggregate. Rare or weakly supported candidates constitute an observable reversal, and learned embeddings recover some of these links that the vote misses. The result permits neither clinical recommendation nor general elimination of learned methods.

In MAUDE, comparison of procedures and diagnosis of a step are separate: a real aggregation structure outperforms degree-preserving rewiring under the fixed settings, but increasing fanout does not ensure a gain and BPR smoothing has a variable effect. This suggests retaining a useful simple step before making it more complex, without establishing an optimal architecture or the causal role of medical relations. Embeddings and labels remain relational in the controls.

In CMS, the tested aggregates do not add a consistent gain over local history, and the documentary proxy does not restore it. Redundancy, limited coverage, inadequate representation, and retrospective availability remain compatible explanations; this study does not identify them causally. A conditional gain bound and sensitivity to a proxy are more informative than a merely similar score, but do not amount to external ownership ground truth.

The cross-domain conclusion is therefore not ``graphs do not help.'' The unit, observable candidates, prior support, and step exploiting links must be specified, then one must check whether its additional complexity changes the ranking at the budget considered. An aggregate metric may conceal systematic reversals; reduced training loss does not guarantee the best recall. All these explanations remain exploratory on periods already consulted.

sections.heading: Limitations and conditions for confirmation
sections.latex:
The comparisons do not exhaustively separate individual history, popularity, and relations. Part D uses history to define its candidates; BPR/GraphSAGE learn links and differ in the implemented objective, negatives, initialization, and auxiliary specialty information. MAUDE controls remove propagation or modify adjacency, not all relational learning. Six configurations do not equalize costs, and the retained parameters do not cover all possible methods.

Event dates do not prove public availability at the origin; registries are incomplete and subject to correction. New Part D relations are observable publications subject to suppression, not first prescriptions. MAUDE codes are not individual diagnoses. CMS inspections are a selected population and the task is conditional on their taking place. The administrative proxy does not certify actual ownership; its absent intermediate groups limit discrimination of mechanisms.

Intervals are conditional on fits/configurations and the specified resampling, without selection coverage or guarantees concerning dependence between networks/periods, and without a simultaneous guarantee. The margin 0.01 is not clinical; subgroup reversals are exploratory. Costs include the actually executed scope, on a shared machine and with uncontrolled caches. A workload of proposals is neither measured human time nor patient benefit.

The Q2 Part D forecast remains sealed and distinct; no Part D 2025 target file or metric for that target is acquired here. Its future evaluation would not automatically confirm the new RC3.1 comparators. These require a distinct protocol before an unconsulted target, snapshots actually available at the origin, and genuine independent attestations/participants. A study by an external team, human relevance of proposals, and author approvals remain unperformed. CMS 2026 is not certified as untouched. The exploratory delivery is technically closed without converting these missing prerequisites into confirmations or negative results.

supplement.heading: Provenance, derived inputs, and limits to reproduction
supplement.latex:
The scientific protocol and its sources were published before launch under commit \nolinkurl{dde6a2facf83a493c23ea4797ff5da9e90138452}, draft PR 7, after successful CI. The protocol SHA-256 is \nolinkurl{faf881cf4a5880f5f444d11badc5ea3a79a08325efb4be394e9c5093137064a8}. The 44 synthetic regression tests and CLI preflight are checks of the new software surface, not scientific or clinical confirmation. The previously successful gradient and scientific audits were not rerun.

Part D and MAUDE consume the retained Q2 preparations, explicitly derived. CMS consumes the seven sources already acquired and verifies the ordered identity of the 23\,712 episodes with the Q2 baseline. Selected BPR states, their outputs, and metadata are retained; new compatibility checks verify their consumption, without retraining. The companion TAR retains actual RC3.1 outputs and retained inputs, separately from the manuscript ZIP. Small Part D BPR selection metadata is delivered separately in the ZIP, under \texttt{data/reused\_inputs/partd\_selection.json}, and is not in that TAR; it does not turn Part D/MAUDE preparations into new raw acquisitions. Availability of public sources and archives to a third party must be checked in practice.

The scientific sources actually consumed are pinned, rather than a package version alone. The code and compact evidence identify the calculations; a clean clone/wheel and reproduction by an external team have not been demonstrated by this new environment. Files from the RC3 parent remain under \texttt{history/RC3}, without retroactive updates to their results, intervals, or PDF certificates.

supplement.heading: Exact scope of interventions and strata
supplement.latex:
Changing MAUDE fanout preserves dimension and trainable parameters, but changes computation and the neighborhood actually aggregated. Rewiring preserves degrees at the annual cutoff and modifies only aggregation adjacency; training labels remain the true links. A single bounded rewiring procedure, with seed 303, is used at each origin: the intervals condition on this realization and do not cover an ensemble of null graphs. They measure no medical causal effect.

The raw--smoothed BPR contrast retains the learned tensors and modifies their use at inference. The configuration was selected with smoothing; this is neither separate selection of the best raw/smoothed models nor removal of all relational learning. Likewise, GraphSAGE without propagation retains an objective trained on links and trainable node vectors. The historical results of this control do not become a relation-free experiment.

The CMS proxy measures the presence of dated administrative support available in the files. It does not provide an external label of valid ownership or an incorrect link. The none/some/all associations retained groups describe its coverage; performance sensitivity may result from coverage, sparsity, or proxy bias and does not causally distinguish link quality from redundant information.

Candidate and neighbor support are measured in the past; recall in these strata concerns observed future positives belonging to each stratum. Zero neighbor support in the fixed Part D top50 cosine stratifier is not an absence of all relations: a method selecting more than fifty neighbors may exploit neighbors outside this stratifier. Thresholds and all strata are retained, not chosen according to favorable contrasts. Generalization to nodes absent from the annual MAUDE fit is not evaluated separately.

supplement.heading: Conditional intervals, seed ranges, and observable workload
supplement.latex:
Each ranking contrast aligns entity--periods, candidates, and positives. Seed results are averaged at the hit level before the micro ratio; they are not three independent observations of each prescriber or product. Paired resampling is by entity and keeps its periods together. For CMS, episodes with the same CCN remain together. Weighted AUCs treat ties as half-pairs. Draws without sufficient classes or denominator invent neither a zero score nor an interval.

Bootstrap percentiles condition on fixed procedures and predictions; they do not retrain, reselect configurations, or cover prior exposure to tests. Relational data and periods may remain dependent beyond the clusters; there is no simultaneous guarantee across all contrasts. Min--max ranges across seeds are descriptive and reported separately. The absolute margin 0.01 is analytical, not a clinical justification by those responsible for the study; conditionally excluding this positive gain does not establish general equivalence.

Overall precision uses all slots proposed to eligible units, including those without positives. Coverage counts entity--periods in which at least one observable positive is recovered. Candidate strata report recall among their positives; no recommendation precision by these strata is claimed from an analysis that does not load all recommendations. The TAR nevertheless retains top100 recommendations and complete scores/ranks.

Curves by $K$ are counts of proposals and recovered published links. They measure neither clinical errors, review minutes, relevance judged by a professional, nor patient benefit. For CMS, measurements remain on retained inspection episodes and do not rank all facilities at a national origin.

supplement.heading: Measured costs and unmet human prerequisites
supplement.latex:
The supervised caps are 1\,800 s, 4 GiB aggregate controller--worker RSS, and 1 GiB of outputs per phase, 3\,600 s of validation per family, and 21\,600 s and 8 GiB of outputs for the run. One numerical thread is enforced. The machine is shared; caches and compilation are not controlled as in a dedicated hardware benchmark. Phase times include their actual software scope. BPR reuse rows exclude the cost of historical training: they do not prove that training BPR costs zero. A vote without learned parameters still retains histories, indexes, and neighbor lists; zero learned parameters does not mean zero memory or computation.

The Q2 Part D forecast retains its protocol, origin, and scores: the new RC3.1 comparators are not added retroactively. The official metadata capture on 4 October 2026 at 19:58:26.587211 UTC, HTTP 200, did not list service year 2025 in the filtered response; this does not establish a universal absence of data. No Part D 2025 target file was acquired or evaluated here. Human non-consultation is unknown. Any RC3.1 confirmation requires a new protocol and sealed scores before a genuinely unconsulted target, with actual snapshot availability and a genuine independent participant. CMS 2026 is not certified as untouched.

A study by an external human team remains unperformed. It must obtain the sources itself, actually reproduce a procedure, add its comparator, retain logs/errors/costs, and distinguish autonomy from assistance. The assistant and review agent are not these participants. Any study of relevance and review time also requires genuine participants, reference judgments, and authorizations.

The data are public administrative/regulatory data; professional and organizational identifiers may remain present. Authors, affiliations, CRediT, funding/conflicts, ethics and data use, AI disclosure, manuscript license, exact publication medium, and approval to submit remain subject to human validation. Technical preparation presumes neither an ethics exemption nor compliance with a journal. No merge, tag, Zenodo publication, or automatic submission is performed. D2 and ClinicalTrials remain out of scope.
